headline: Auto growth can't offset handset weakness and margin squeeze
summary_short: Revenue for the quarter ended June 28, 2026 fell 4.0% y/y to $9.95B as a 20% handset decline outweighed 61% automotive growth; diluted EPS dropped 23.0% y/y to $1.87 amid semiconductor input-cost pressure.
summary_long: Revenue fell 4.0% y/y to $9.95B as QCT handset revenue dropped 20% y/y to $5.09B, only partly offset by automotive (+61% to $1.59B, a 23rd straight quarter of double-digit growth) and IoT (+9%). Gross margin compressed 2.5ppt y/y to 53.1% and operating margin fell 10.3ppt to 16.3% as management cited industry-wide increases in wafer, assembly, test, packaging, and memory input costs, which it says pricing actions will offset over time. Net income fell 24.9% y/y to $2.00B and diluted EPS fell 23.0% to $1.87. Cash fell to $4.53B; long-term debt declined to $12.78B. Qualcomm returned $2.3B to shareholders ($973M dividends, $1.4B buybacks). Q4 FY2026 guidance: revenue $9.7-10.5B, non-GAAP diluted EPS $2.05-2.25.

drivers.explanation: QCT handset revenue fell 20% y/y to $5.09B, more than offsetting automotive (+61% to $1.59B) and IoT (+9% to $1.83B); QTL licensing revenue was roughly flat (-3%).

CEO cited a 'challenging memory and supply environment' and industry-wide input-cost increases across wafer fab, assembly, test, packaging and memory; pricing actions to offset this are only gradually taking effect.
QCT segment EBT margin fell 4ppt y/y to 26% and QTL fell 2ppt to 69%, tracking the same input-cost pressure cited for gross margin, plus R&D spend up 17% y/y.
Tracks the EBT decline (-17% y/y) plus a higher tax expense ($460M vs $286M y/y); not explained further in the release beyond the segment margin commentary.
Tracks the net-income decline; diluted share count also fell 2.7% y/y on buybacks, a small partial offset.
Tax expense of $460M on $2,462M pretax income (18.7%) vs $286M on $2,952M (9.7%) a year ago; the release does not state a cause for the prior-year quarter's unusually low rate.

CEO framed the quarter as 'solid execution... despite a challenging memory and supply environment,' pointing to the Investor Day non-handset growth targets (to $40B by FY2029) and the closed Modular Inc acquisition as forward strategic context.
